description:

Our client, a family-owned property investment business: four companies, around 90 properties across London, Liverpool and the rest of the UK. The administrator will keep the office, the paperwork and the money flowing smoothly.
Responsibilities:
Accounts Admin
- Collect supplier invoices and utility bills as they arrive by email and post. Download bills from supplier portals.
- Check each invoice against the order, contract or agreement. Send queries to whoever placed the order.
- Rename and file every invoice using the company's expense codes, by company and property.
- Prepare the weekly payment run for approval. Approved payments are made by James or Kate; the administrator does not authorise payments.
- Load payroll and PAYE payments from the figures the bookkeeper provides.
- Send the week's invoices to the bookkeeper on a set day and keep the reference copy filed.
- Keep the bank account and supplier details list up to date and confirm any change of supplier bank details by phone before it is used.
- Act as the bookkeeper's day-to-day contact for missing invoices, receipts and queries.
- Help set up and apply the new cost codes, so every cost is allocated to a property and a company.
- Gather the information needed for VAT returns, year-end accounts and confirmation statements, to the deadlines in the calendar.

Combined Calendar
Set up and run one calendar for the whole business, with reminders far enough ahead to act on:
- Accounts: VAT returns, annual accounts, confirmation statements and payroll dates, each with a preparation window before it.
- Property: rent due dates, rent reviews, lease breaks and expiries, and tenancy renewals.
- Compliance: gas safety, electrical, fire risk, EPC and other certificates, licences and inspections.
- Insurance: renewal dates.
- People: HR dates such as probation reviews and annual reviews.

Insurance Admin
- Keep the insurance schedule up to date: policies, renewal dates, premiums and documents.
- Be the brokers' day-to-day contact for documents, changes and renewals.
- Tell the brokers in writing about changes such as vacant units, changes of use and building works, as directed.
- Keep the claims file in order.
- Review policy documents and make sure their terms and conditions are kept to, for example inspections of vacant units, heating and water rules, tenant referencing and electrical safety reports. Diarise each condition and flag anything not being met.

Office, Post and Records
- Clear the backlog of paper records in the office: sort, scan where useful, file, and send to storage.
- Set up and keep a retention and destruction schedule for stored records, on the accountant's advice.
- Keep the office running: supplies, equipment, deliveries and visitors.
- Help with the office move in May 2027.

Company and Legal Administration
- Keep company records up to date for the four companies and prepare Companies House filings for approval.
- Keep registers of leases, tenancies, licences and key documents, and know where the originals are.

HR Admin
- Keep staff files: contracts, right-to-work checks, holiday and absence records.
- Diarise probation and annual reviews, and help prepare them.
- Help with recruitment admin: adverts, CVs, interview scheduling and onboarding.
- Keep HR policies filed and up to date, with the HR adviser.

IT & Systems
- Be the day-to-day contact for the IT provider: new users, laptops, access and faults.
- Help move files into the new shared document system and keep its folders tidy.

title: Community Data Administrator
description:
About us

We are a leading integrated media and marketing services company at the heart of a community of over 590,000 UK healthcare professionals. With more than 30 years of experience, we produce industry-leading content and experiences through our award-winning brands, publications, and events. We produce trusted, data-driven content that informs and inspires healthcare professionals across the UK and Europe. We are a Great Place to Work and UK's Best Workplaces for Women certified employer, offering a range of benefits including 28 days annual leave (rising to 30 days after 2 years) excluding bank holidays, private healthcare insurance, flexible working and more.

The Role

Our Community Data Administrator will be responsible for the quality, coverage, depth and development of the organisation's HCP community. The role will ensure we have a high-quality, accurate, comprehensive, current, relevant and growing audience that meets the needs of the business and our clients.

They will develop a detailed understanding of the organisation's HCP data and the wider addressable HCP market, identifying where we have strong coverage, where gaps exist and what actions we can take to address them. They will use first- and third-party data, market intelligence and behavioural and engagement data to understand the composition and health of our community and identify opportunities for growth and improvement.

This is a highly analytical role for someone who loves working with data, numbers and solving problems. They will interrogate datasets, spot patterns and anomalies, assess data quality and freshness, identify gaps and translate findings into clear actions.

Working closely with teams across the organisation, they will help source and evaluate new data, improve HCP profiling and segmentation, strengthen our understanding of audience engagement and ensure our HCP community becomes increasingly accurate, complete, current and commercially valuable.

Location: Central London (Hybrid)

Reporting to: Digital Director

Expected start date: January 2027

Salary: £30,000 to £38,000 per annum, depending on experience

Key Responsibilities:

Data Quality & Governance

Take ownership of the overall health of the organisation's HCP database, including accuracy, completeness, recency, duplication, consistency, consent and compliance. Establish clear definitions and standards for data quality and regularly measure the database against them, including agreed definitions for active HCPs, inactive HCPs, dormant records, complete profiles and verified HCPs. Identify data quality issues and work with relevant teams to implement solutions and continually improve the reliability of our data.

HCP Coverage & Gap Analysis

Build a detailed understanding of the organisation's coverage of the HCP market and identify gaps by profession, specialty, geography, seniority and other relevant characteristics. Develop clear, data-led plans to address priority audience gaps and measure the impact of actions taken.

Data Enrichment

Identify opportunities to enhance existing HCP records with additional data points and attributes, improving the completeness and depth of our profiles. Determine which additional attributes would provide the greatest audience, editorial and commercial value and identify appropriate sources for obtaining them.

Data Freshness & Engagement

Assess how recently and frequently HCPs interact with the organisation across our brands, websites, newsletters, events, CPD platforms, surveys and other products. Develop and maintain an HCP engagement scoring methodology that combines behavioural signals across the business to provide a consistent view of audience engagement. Use engagement and recency data to understand the active audience within our overall community and identify opportunities to increase engagement.

Audience Re-engagement & Cleansing

Identify inactive, ageing, duplicate, incomplete or low-confidence records. Work with relevant teams to determine appropriate approaches for re-engagement, verification, consolidation, suppression or removal. Monitor the effectiveness of re-engagement and cleansing activity and use the findings to continually improve our approach.

Data Matching & Deduplication

Develop approaches for identifying duplicate HCP records and matching individuals across different the organisation datasets, platforms and data sources. Investigate conflicting information and establish appropriate rules for determining the most reliable and current information. Support the development of an increasingly consistent and accurate single view of each HCP across the organisation.

Segmentation & Audience Insight

Develop meaningful HCP segments based on profession, specialty, geography, seniority, demographics, behaviour, engagement, recency and other relevant characteristics. Analyse these segments to identify patterns, opportunities and changes in audience behaviour. Translate complex data into clear insights that can be understood and acted upon by teams across the business.

Data Acquisition & Gap Closure

Research and evaluate new first- and third-party data sources that could strengthen the organisation's HCP community. Assess potential sources based on quality, coverage, accuracy, recency, compliance, cost and likely incremental value. Develop data-led recommendations for acquiring or generating data to address identified audience gaps and measure whether those interventions successfully improve coverage.

Commercial Audience Analysis

Work closely with Sales and other commercial teams to understand current and emerging client audience requirements. Translate these requirements into data needs and assess the organisation's ability to reach relevant HCP audiences. Identify areas where strengthening our data could create new commercial opportunities or improve our existing audience proposition.

Measurement & Reporting

Develop and maintain reporting on the health and development of the organisation's HCP community. Monitor key metrics including database size, net growth, coverage, completeness, duplication, freshness, active and inactive audiences, engagement and enrichment. Move beyond simply reporting numbers by identifying what the data tells us, highlighting emerging issues and opportunities and making clear recommendations for action.

HCP Data Expertise

Become the organisation's internal authority on our HCP community. Develop a comprehensive understanding of what data we hold, where it comes from, how reliable and current it is, how our audiences engage with the organisation, where gaps exist and what opportunities there are to improve the data. Support teams across the business with questions about HCP audience size, composition, coverage and engagement.

About You

We're looking for someone who is naturally curious and genuinely enjoys working with data. You'll have a highly analytical mind, an exceptional eye for detail and a tendency to ask "why?" and "what does this tell us?" rather than simply accepting numbers at face value.

You'll enjoy getting into the detail of datasets, spotting patterns, gaps and inconsistencies and working out how to solve them. You'll be organised, methodical and comfortable working with large volumes of data, while also being able to step back and understand the bigger picture.

Most importantly, you'll be someone who lives and breathes data - excited by numbers, curious about what they can tell us and always looking for ways to make the organisation's HCP community better, more current and more valuable.

How to Apply

If you would like to join a progressive company with excellent career prospects and want to be part of our journey, then we are looking forward to hearing from you! Please send a CV and cover letter to Bianca Pettifor on (url removed) or apply below.

Please note that due to the expected high numbers of applications, we are able to only contact successful candidates. Also, while there is no application deadline for this role, interviews will be arranged as and when suitable candidates apply and we reserve the right to close applications at any time once a successful candidate has been selected. No recruitment agencies please.

description:

- Proven experience using the ADP payroll platform is essential.

- Excellent attention to detail and a high level of numerical accuracy.
- Strong organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and meet tight deadlines.
- High levels of discretion and integrity when handling confidential and sensitive employee information.
- A proactive, flexible and collaborative approach to working within a small team.

Qualifications

Working closely with the Buying and Marketplace teams, you will play an important role in supporting new sellers and getting their products successfully set up on the Marketplace. What We're Looking For

This role would suit someone early in their career who is keen to develop within buying administration, e-commerce or marketplace operations. You may have 0-2 years' experience, or have developed relevant skills through university, internships, placements, customer service or a similar role.

- A genuine interest in retail, buying, e-commerce and online marketplaces.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

- Excellent attention to detail and the ability to work accurately with product information and data.
- The ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively to deadlines.

- The ability to work effectively with technical, operational and commercial teams.
- Familiarity with product listings, supplier platforms or marketplace tools would be advantageous, but isn't essential.

Why Join?

This is a great opportunity to join a growing retail business with an expanding e-commerce and Marketplace operation.

You'll gain exposure to a broad range of buying, product administration, supplier communication and commercial activities, developing an understanding of how products are brought onto a retail platform and managed successfully.

For someone looking to build a career within buying, merchandising or e-commerce, this role offers a strong foundation and the opportunity to develop within an established retail business.

Identify data quality issues and work with relevant teams to implement solutions and continually improve the reliability of our data.

HCP Coverage & Gap Analysis

Data Enrichment

Identify opportunities to enhance existing HCP records with additional data points and attributes, improving the completeness and depth of our profiles. Data Freshness & Engagement

Assess how recently and frequently HCPs interact with the organisation across our brands, websites, newsletters, events, CPD platforms, surveys and other products. Audience Re-engagement & Cleansing

Work with relevant teams to determine appropriate approaches for re-engagement, verification, consolidation, suppression or removal. Data Matching & Deduplication

Develop approaches for identifying duplicate HCP records and matching individuals across different the organisation datasets, platforms and data sources. Investigate conflicting information and establish appropriate rules for determining the most reliable and current information. Support the development of an increasingly consistent and accurate single view of each HCP across the organisation.

Segmentation & Audience Insight

Develop meaningful HCP segments based on profession, specialty, geography, seniority, demographics, behaviour, engagement, recency and other relevant characteristics. Analyse these segments to identify patterns, opportunities and changes in audience behaviour. Translate complex data into clear insights that can be understood and acted upon by teams across the business.

Research and evaluate new first- and third-party data sources that could strengthen the organisation's HCP community. Assess potential sources based on quality, coverage, accuracy, recency, compliance, cost and likely incremental value. Develop data-led recommendations for acquiring or generating data to address identified audience gaps and measure whether those interventions successfully improve coverage.

title: Trainee HR Administrator
description:
Thinking About a Career Change? Why Not Choose HR?

If you've reached a crossroads in your professional life and are looking for a fresh start in a people-focused, rewarding industry then Human Resources might be exactly what you're looking for.

Many of our candidates come from diverse professional backgrounds retail, customer service, administration, healthcare, education, hospitality, and more. What they all have in common is the desire to do meaningful work, support others, and build a stable, long-term career.

Our HR Career Change Programme

We specialise in helping individuals transition into HR-starting with recognised qualifications and ending with real job opportunities.

Whether you're working full-time, part-time, or in between roles, our online learning and personalised recruitment support can help you make a successful move into the HR profession often in just a few months.

Please note that this is a training course and fees apply.

Why Human Resources?

The HR profession is growing steadily across all sectors. As businesses put more focus on employee wellbeing, development, and company culture, skilled HR professionals are more important than ever.

Even entry-level roles in HR offer strong salaries, clear progression routes, and opportunities to specialise over time (in areas like learning & development, recruitment, employee relations, and more).

Here are typical UK salaries at various stages of the HR journey:
- HR Administrator - £27,000+
- HR Assistant - £30,000+
- HR Officer - £35,000+
- HR Advisor - £38,500+
- HR Manager - £55,000+

And with hybrid and remote roles increasingly common in HR, the flexibility is there too.

How It Works - Your 3 Step Journey Into HR

Step 1 - CIPD Level 3 Certificate in People Practice

The CIPD Level 3 Certificate in People Practice is the industry-standard entry point into Human Resources. It's assignment-based (no exams), and is delivered fully online with expert tutor support.
- Accredited by the Chartered Institute of Personnel & Development (CIPD)
- Covers recruitment, employee relations, HR systems, and more
- Complete in approx. 10-12 weeks at your own pace

This course not only boosts your employability-it also gives you the confidence and credibility to take the leap into a new industry.

title: Content Coordinator
description:
This is a newly created, part-time contract role (three days a week), designed to bring structure, coordination and administrative discipline to ExchangeWire's content function. The Content Coordinator keeps the team running smoothly, looks after all content administration and keeps agreed processes on track. The right person is highly organised, proactive and comfortable working across teams and with part-time, remote staff.

Role Overview

The Content Coordinator works day to day with the Head of Content and closely with the COO, who is the point of escalation. The role covers the operational coordination of the content team:
- The editorial calendar and content schedule
- Workflow between content and other departments
- Content admin and tracking
- Client and contributor communications
- Coordination with the two part-time admin staff

Content operations & scheduling

Editorial calendar & scheduling
- Work with the Head of Content to maintain the editorial calendar, so that all content (sponsored and non-sponsored) is tracked from commission to publication.
- Keep track of the content pipeline and flag gaps, delays or conflicts to the Head of Content.
- Coordinate scheduling across written, audio and video formats to support a balanced, consistent output.
- Maintain tracking documents for all live content projects.

Process compliance
- Track whether agreed content production processes are being followed, including by freelancers, and flag any departures to the Head of Content.
- Act as the checkpoint between content creation and publication, so that no tasks or deliverables are overlooked.
- Identify process inefficiencies and raise them with the Head of Content or COO, along with proposed improvements.

Client & contributor communications

A key aspect of this role is ensuring that communication with clients and contributors is maintained and upheld.

Sponsored content comms
- On confirmation of a sponsored content deal, take ownership of initial outreach to the client: introduce the process, set expectations and confirm timelines.
- Manage ongoing communication with content clients throughout production, including chasing assets, providing updates and escalating blockers.
- Maintain a clear log of all active sponsored content projects and their status.

AV & multimedia comms (with the Multimedia Editor)
- Work closely with the Multimedia Editor so that guest and contributor communications for podcast and video content are handled in a timely and professional manner.
- Track guest confirmations, recording logistics and post-production communications for all AV formats.

Cross-functional coordination

Marketing interface

The Content Coordinator is the primary point of contact for marketing when they need content assets, scheduling support or publication assistance, and makes sure their requests are prioritised and actioned within agreed timelines. They also take part in the weekly cross-team meeting and maintain shared status updates.

Sales handover management

The Content Coordinator receives and tracks sponsored content handovers from the sales team, acknowledges receipt and communicates timelines to both the sales team and the client. They then monitor delivery against commitments and flag any at-risk projects early.

Team admin & coordination

The Content Coordinator works closely with ExchangeWire's two part-time admin staff, so that admin tasks are clearly allocated, understood and completed on time.

They coordinate regularly with both admin staff on priorities and deadlines, agree with the Head of Content how content-related admin tasks are allocated, and track those tasks through to completion. Any capacity issues or blockers are escalated to the Head of Content promptly.

General team admin

The Content Coordinator also maintains shared team documentation, keeps internal tracking tools up to date, and supports the Head of Content with client and internal reporting and performance data as required.

Skills & experience

Essential
- Demonstrable experience in an operations, coordination or project management role, ideally within media, publishing or B2 B.
- Exceptional organisational skills.
- Strong written communication skills.
- Confident working across teams and with senior stakeholders.
- Comfortable in a small business environment.
- Ability to be flexible, hands-on and autonomous.
- Able to work as an independent contractor (own limited company or sole trader) and invoice monthly.

Desirable
- Familiarity with the digital advertising or ad tech industry.
- Experience working with CMS platforms, project management tools and shared editorial calendars.
- Experience with client management.
- Previous experience working on a freelance or contract basis.

The business provides a modern technology platform that helps organisations manage risk, compliance and governance more effectively. Working with recognised brands across financial services, retail, technology, energy and professional services, the company is continuing to grow its presence in the market.

Alongside its technology platform, the business is developing a professional network that brings together industry experts to share knowledge, exchange ideas and build meaningful connections.

With an established membership of over 500 professionals, the ambition is to grow this into a leading community for risk and compliance professionals across the UK and beyond.

This is where you come in.

This is a varied, hands-on opportunity for someone with an interest in content, social media, events and community building.

You'll take ownership of the day-to-day running and development of the community, looking after memberships, coordinating content, driving engagement and helping deliver a programme of online and in-person events.

One day you could be writing a newsletter and managing social content; the next, coordinating an industry webinar, briefing speakers or organising an in-person networking event.

You'll work closely with teams across marketing, sales, product and customer success, giving you exposure to the wider business and the opportunity to shape how the community develops.

Key Responsibilities
- Manage day-to-day community membership, welcoming new members and responding to queries.
- Coordinate content calendars, newsletters, social posts and community discussions.

- Manage the community platform, ensuring content remains relevant, active and up to date.
- Support the delivery of webinars, industry panels, networking events and customer events.
- Coordinate event logistics, including venues, speakers, invitations, materials and post-event follow-up.
- Track membership growth, content engagement and event performance, using insights to improve future activity.
- Collaborate with internal teams to connect community activity with wider business and customer objectives.
- Bring fresh ideas for growing the community and take ownership of putting them into action.

About You

You could be a recent graduate or have 1-2 years' experience in social media, content, marketing, events or community management.

What matters most is your attitude, communication skills and ability to take ownership.

You'll ideally bring:
- Strong written communication skills, with the ability to create engaging social posts, newsletters and professional communications.
- Confidence adapting your tone of voice across different audiences and platforms.
- A genuine interest in bringing people together and building professional relationships.
- Experience organising events, managing social channels, creating content or growing an online community.
- Excellent organisation and attention to detail, particularly when managing multiple projects and deadlines.
- Confidence engaging with senior professionals, hosting conversations and representing a business at events.
- A proactive mindset, with plenty of ideas and the drive to see them through.
- An interest in learning, developing and building something from the ground up.

Experience with community platforms, social scheduling tools and email marketing software would be advantageous, but isn't essential.

You don't need previous experience in risk or compliance. The business will provide the opportunity to learn the sector and develop your knowledge.

Why Join?
- Ownership from day one: Play a central role in developing an established professional community.
- Room to grow: An opportunity to develop your responsibilities as the community expands.
- Business exposure: Work across marketing, sales, product and customer success.
- Networking: Build relationships with senior professionals from recognised UK

Rates depend on experience and client requirements

title: Accounts Payable Coordinator
description:

title: Interim Income and Funding Finance Assistant
description:
The Income and Funding Assistant is responsible for supporting the Finance Department in maintaining accurate accounting records and managing income processes for schools and college centres. This role ensures the delivery of a robust, efficient, and effective finance function across the organisation, while working collaboratively with on-site teams to provide timely and high-quality financial and income-related support

Client Details

Leading South London/Surrey Education and Charitable organisation are seeking an Income and Funding Finance Assistant on an initial six-month contract basis. This job may become permanent.

Description
- Work closely with individual schools and college centres to ensure all required Arbor MIS data is collected, validated, reviewed, and submitted within agreed timelines and in accordance with Trust Finance Regulations and Procedures.
- Conduct detailed reviews of Arbor MIS pupil and place-led data to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency, investigating and resolving discrepancies with schools and Local Authorities.
- Maintain comprehensive student-level income reconciliations, comparing funding received against pupil records, Education Health and Care Plans (EHCPs), place funding allocations, grant schedules, and Local Authority remittances.
- Produce monthly school-level income reconciliations and funding movement reports, highlighting variances, anomalies, and escalating potential financial risks.
- Perform detailed monthly income analysis across all income streams, including High Needs funding, grants, lettings, recoupment income, bursaries, and other traded activities.
- Analyse funding trends, pupil number movements, occupancy levels, and funding variances to identify risks, opportunities, and areas requiring management intervention.
- Prepare monthly income reports and dashboards for Finance Business Partners and senior management, providing commentary on key movements, variances, and financial performance.
- Support income forecasting and budget monitoring processes by providing accurate income projections and trend analysis.
- Utilise Sage and invoicing systems to ensure invoices are raised accurately, coded correctly, and processed in accordance with Trust procedures and timescales.
- Raise invoices for Local Authority top-up funding, DfE grants, lettings income, recoupment charges, outreach services, and other income-generating activities.
- Monitor invoice workflows and resolve invoice discrepancies promptly, ensuring compliance with financial controls and audit requirements.
- Accurately process and post all bank transactions on a timely basis.
- Maintain cashbook records and ensure all receipts and payments are appropriately coded and recorded.
- Prepare monthly bank reconciliations for schools, college centres, and the Trust, investigating and resolving any unreconciled items promptly.
- Prepare monthly income accruals, deferred income calculations, and journal postings in accordance with accounting standards and Trust procedures.
- Support month-end and year-end reporting processes by ensuring income transactions are accurately recorded and reconciled.

Profile

A successful Interim Income And Funding Finance Assistant should have:
- AAT qualified or studying towards a recognised accounting qualification (desirable).
- Proven experience in a finance role with responsibility for sales ledger, income management, reconciliations, and financial reporting.
- Experience within the education, academy, public sector, or not-for-profit environment is desirable.
- Experience working with Local Authority funding arrangements, grants, or educational funding streams would be advantageous.
- Strong working knowledge of Sage Accounting Software, Arbor MIS, and financial management systems.
- Advanced Microsoft Excel skills including:
- Pivot Tables
- VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP
- SUMIFS
- INDEX MATCH
- Data validation
- Power Query (desirable)
- Strong understanding of sales ledger processes, credit control, cashbook management, and bank reconciliations.
- Sound knowledge of accruals, prepayments, deferred income, journals, and financial controls.
- Ability to analyse large data sets and convert financial information into meaningful management reports.
- Strong analytical and investigative skills with the ability to identify trends, anomalies, and opportunities from financial data.
- Ability to interpret complex funding information and reconcile multiple data sources accurately.
- Experience producing financial analysis, variance reports, KPI reporting, and forecasting information.
- Ability to challenge data, identify root causes of discrepancies, and recommend practical solutions.
- Strong attention to detail with a commitment to data integrity and accuracy.

Job Offer
- Temporary Interim Income And Funding Finance Assistant contract in Sutton.
- Hourly pay of £20 to £24, dependent on the level of experience.

- Good understanding of double-entry bookkeeping and balance sheet controls.

title: Credit Controller
description:
Reed are working with a leading healthcare business based in Central Croydon. We have been approached to support them with their aim to hire a new Credit Controller who will work within a dedicated finance team of 5.

The business is considered one of the leaders in their market, and have been in operation for over 30 years and provides a range of care services across the UK. You will be joining a growing and expanding business with an excellent reputation in the sector it operates.

As an experienced Credit Controller, your role will be to support the business in managing the company's credit, and ensuring timely payments, to support smooth financial operations and a healthy cashflow across their services and ensure accurate billing and invoicing for local authorities, private clients and other stakeholders. As the newly appointed Credit Controller you will manage credit control processes with professionalism, empathy and ideally with an understanding of the regulatory and operational environment within care (this industry sector is not essential).

As the newly appointed Credit Controller, your duties and responsibilities will include :
- Proactively chase outstanding payments in accordance with agreed credit terms.
- Maintain regular communication with commissioners, finance teams, and private clients to ensure timely settlements.
- Monitor aged debt reports, highlight risks, and recommend actions to senior management.
- Implement and maintain robust credit control processes to minimise bad debt.
- Negotiate payment plans where appropriate and escalate overdue accounts when necessary.
- Prepare and issue accurate weekly/monthly invoices for local authorities, NHS bodies, private funders, and self-pay clients.
- Validate care delivery records, fee changes, and funding arrangements prior to billing.
- Ensure compliance with contract terms, frameworks, and commissioning requirements.
- Maintain up-to-date records of service users, funding sources, and billing cycles.
- Investigate and resolve invoice discrepancies quickly and effectively.

To be considered for the Credit Controller position, your background, skillsets and experience will include :
- Proven experience as a Credit Controller ideally within the care, healthcare, or social services sector, although this is not essential.
- Strong knowledge of billing cycles, invoicing processes, and debt management.
- Excellent communication skills with the ability to maintain professional and empathetic relationships.
- Strong IT skills, including finance systems and Excel.
- High level of accuracy, organisation, and attention to detail.

This role is based out of our client's Central Croydon office with a hybrid working model available of 3 days in the office, and 2 days working remotely. A salary between £40,000 & £45,000 per annum is available, dependent on experience.

title: Recovery & Opportunities Coordinator
description:
Single Homeless Project has an opportunity for a Recovery & Opportunities Coordinator to join our experienced and committed teams based in Islington . You will join us on a full-time, permanent basis. In return, you will receive a competitive salary starting at £29,822.41 and rising incrementally to £32,034.46 per annum.

We re London s leading homelessness charity and we get things done.

In a city where hundreds are forced into homelessness every day, our work has never been more needed or more challenging. And we re not shying away. We re rolling up our sleeves to make change and helping over 10,000 Londoners every year. We prevent homelessness, provide safe places to live and give people the opportunity to rebuild their lives and transform their futures. And we never give up.

We re here for Londoners wherever they are on their journey. We start with trust, building relationships that help people feel safe, supported, and ready to move forward. Every day, we put people first in everything we do, challenging injustice and barriers that keep people from the safety, stability and opportunity they deserve. We stand alongside people as they rebuild and shape a future that feels their own.

Joining Single Homeless Project means joining a team that s bold, compassionate and determined to do better for the people we support and for each other. You ll work alongside colleagues with lived experience, in a space that s trans-inclusive, disability-friendly, and actively striving to be anti-oppressive and equitable.

We re not perfect, but we re real. We listen. We learn. And we push forward, together. Because this isn t just a job. It s a chance to lead with empathy, spark change, and help build a London where no one is left behind.

About the Recovery & Opportunities Coordinator role:

Recovery looks different for everyone, and meaningful opportunities can be a powerful part of helping people move forward. As a Recovery and Opportunities Coordinator, you ll take the lead in creating a programme that gives clients across Ashley Road, Milton House and Highbury New Park the chance to build confidence, strengthen their wellbeing, discover new interests, develop new skills and take positive steps towards greater independence.

This is a hands on and creative role where you ll turn ideas into activities that people genuinely want to take part in. You ll design and deliver engaging group work covering areas such as mental and physical health, relationships, substance use, life skills and learning, while creating opportunities that support clients to prepare for moving on to more independent accommodation. You ll use a strengths based and trauma-informed approach, adapting what you offer to respond to people s interests, goals and experiences.

You ll also look beyond our services to create more opportunities for clients. Building strong relationships with community organisations, statutory services, specialist agencies and lived experience networks, you ll help connect people with the resources, activities and support available around them. Alongside this, you ll champion co-production, support colleagues, volunteers and peers to get involved in delivering the programme, and help make recovery and social inclusion a visible part of everyday service delivery.

About you:
- You have experience developing, coordinating and facilitating groups and activities, with a good understanding of group dynamics and how to support others to deliver them confidently and effectively.
- You re creative, enthusiastic and proactive, with the confidence to turn ideas into meaningful opportunities and encourage clients, colleagues, volunteers and peers to get involved.
- You re confident building positive working relationships and partnerships with a range of internal and external services, helping to open up new opportunities for the people we support.
- You understand how to engage, motivate and inspire people experiencing multiple disadvantage, including the barriers that can make participation more difficult, and can create a positive and welcoming atmosphere.
- You re committed to inclusive practice, creating environments where people from different backgrounds feel respected and able to participate, while maintaining clear and appropriate professional boundaries.

Our attractive benefits package includes:
- A salary increase after successfully completing six month's probationary period
- A 37.5 hour working week including flexible working hours (core hours are 10am 4pm) in non-accommodation services
- 25 days annual leave, increasing annually to the maximum 30 days (plus paid Bank Holidays),
- A contributory pension scheme: Single Homeless Project will contribute the equivalent of 5% of your annual salary
- Staff Health Cash Plan and discounts scheme
- Comprehensive and integrated training programme designed specifically to develop the skills and knowledge involved in our work

Don t miss out on this great opportunity to join the Single Homeless Project team please click apply now to become our Recovery & Opportunities Coordinator ? - we'd like to hear from you!

Working relationships The postholder will work closely with: Borough Training Hub Programme Manager Workforce Development Lead Islington Training Hub Clinical Lead NCL Education Faculty Programme Directors and clinical educators Education Faculty & Quality team Islington GP Federation & practices London ICS Training Hub and associated colleagues NHS England Workforce Training Education team

title: Receptionist
description: Essex Lodge Surgery is looking for 2 Part Time experienced GP receptionists Must have excellent communication and customer service skills to join our friendly team The purpose of the role is to: Offer general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone. Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way Undertake a variety of administrative duties to assist in the smooth running of the reception area, including the provision of clerical support to clinical staff and other members of the practice team. Facilitate effective communication between patients, members of the primary health care team, secondary care and other associated healthcare agencies Duties and responsibilities: The duties and responsibilities to be undertaken by members of the reception team may include all of the items in the following list. Duties may be varied from time to time under the direction of the practice manager/partners, dependent on current and evolving practice workload and staffing levels: Maintaining and monitoring the practice appointments system Processing personal and telephone requests for appointments, visits and telephone consultations, and ensuring callers are directed to the appropriate healthcare professional Process appointment requests for today/future appointment from patients in person Using your own judgment and communication skills, ensure that patients with no prior appointment but who need urgent consultation are seen in a logical and non-disruptive manner Receive and make telephone calls as required. Divert calls and take messages, ensuring accuracy of detail and prompt appropriate delivery. Deal with home visit requests Ensure 2 week wait referral are emailed as soon as you receive them, completed tracker and file Ensure 2 week wait folder if checked on a daily basis Patient notes and correspondence: Retrieve and re-file records as required, ensuring strict alphabetical order is adhered to Ensure correspondence, reports, results etc. are filed promptly and in the correct records, ensuring that all recent correspondence is available when patients are seen. Ensure that all new patients are registered onto the computer system promptly and accurately Explain practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover, and ensure procedures are completed Where possible check the contact details for patients, address, contact numbers and recording next of kin details and carers Process patients requests for change of address and contact numbers Enter patient information on to the computer as required Processing and distributing incoming (and outgoing) mail Taking messages and passing on information Managing the surgery's generic email accounts, dealing with requests and forwarding relevant message to other members staff when required Help promote NHS Friends and Family Questionnaires and other initiatives set by CCG and NHS England. Scanning correspondence with accuracy in patients electronic medical records Filing and retrieving paperwork Processing repeat prescriptions in accordance with practice guidelines Handing completed repeat prescription to patients, checking names and addresses Computer data entry/data allocation and collation; processing and recording information in accordance with practice procedures Initiating contact with and responding to requests from patients, other team member and associated healthcare agencies and providers Providing clerical assistance to practice staff as required from time to time, including word/data processing, filing, photocopying and scanning Monitoring of stationery and other clinical supplies to ensure order requests are placed to maintain adequate stock Keeping the reception area, notice-boards and leaflet dispensers tidy and free from obstructions and clutter Undertake any other additional duties appropriate to the post as requested by the partners or the practice manager. Confidentiality: In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately In the performance of the duties outlined in this job description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data Health & safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice health & safety policy, the practice health & safety manual, and the practice infection control policy and published procedures. This will include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way, free from hazards Actively reporting health and safety hazards and infection hazards immediately when recognised Keeping own work areas and general/patient areas generally clean, assisting in the maintenance of general standards of cleanliness consistent with the scope of the job holders role Undertaking periodic infection control training (minimum annually) Reporting potential risks identified Demonstrate due regard for safeguarding and promoting the welfare of vulnerable adults and children Equality and diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognises the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner that is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/professional development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, with such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Ensuring mandatory training is undertaken when required to do so. Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication: The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the implementation of services: The post-holder will Apply practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audits where appropriate Flexibility: This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive description of every duty performed by the receptionist, but rather a guide to the type and nature of the duties. In Essex Lodge Surgery, flexibility in the duties undertaken and the hours worked are essential to achieve the objectives of a smooth running practice. The post holder is required to carry out any duties that fall within the scope of this role, that may reasonably be requested by the Partners or the Practice Manager and that relate to the efficiency and smooth running of the Practice.

title: Receptionist/Administrator
description: We are seeking a professional, organised Receptionist to join the Front of House team at Central London Community Healthcare NHS Trust. As the first point of contact, you will provide a welcoming, efficient and high-quality reception service for patients, visitors and colleagues. You will create a positive experience for service users, demonstrating excellent communication skills, attention to detail and a commitment to outstanding patient care. The role requires the ability to manage competing priorities, remain calm and compassionate under pressure, and use initiative to resolve day-to-day challenges. Strong IT skills are essential, as you will regularly use digital systems to support accurate and efficient service delivery. The successful candidate will be approachable, reliable and able to work effectively as part of a busy healthcare team. Sites include: Bessborough Clinic, SW1V 2JD Colville Health Centre, W11 1PA Emperor's Gate Surgery, SW7 4HJ Lisson Grove Health Centre, NW8 8EG Parkview Centre for Health and Wellbeing, W12 7FG Queen's Park Medical Practice, W10 4LD South Westminster Centre for Health, SW1P 2PF St Charles Centre for Health and Wellbeing, W10 6DZ The Medical Centre, W9 3XZ Violet Melchett Clinic, SW3 5RR World's End Health Centre, SW10 0UD This is an excellent opportunity to contribute to patient care while providing a professional and welcoming front-of-house service across our community healthcare sites. Provide a warm, professional welcome to all service users, directing them to the appropriate departments or services. Ensure all service users are treated with dignity and respect at all times, and that any personal information is communicated with sensitivity, discretion, and professionalism. Ensure all messages, whether via telephone, email, or written notes, are accurately recorded and promptly relayed, seeking clarification when needed. Maintain up-to-date knowledge of all clinics, booking systems, and associated protocols/templates, and proactively suggest improvements where appropriate. Confirm appointments with service users in advance, using telephone or written communication as appropriate. Support the upkeep of a clean and safe environment for all, adhering to fire safety and health and safety guidelines. Work collaboratively with clinical teams to support effective patient flow and service delivery. Provide receptionist cover at other sites when required, maintaining a consistent high standard of service across locations. Applicants are expected to present clear and relevant evidence of the competencies and responsibilities detailed in the attached Job Description and Person Specification, together with a demonstrated commitment to the Trusts values of Accountability, Inclusion, Compassion, and Empowerment.

title: Team Administrator
company: South West London and St Georges Mental Health NHS Trust
advertiser_name: South West London and St Georges Mental Health NHS Trust
description: An opportunity has arisen for a Band 4 Administrator to provide support to the Adult ADHD / ASD Services. The post is based in Jubilee Health Centre, Wallington. The post holder will play a pivotal role in creating, sustaining and supporting the administrative and communication support systems within the services. The post holder will provide an effective and comprehensive range of administrative services to the multi-disciplinary team. The post holder to undertake a varied number of duties to ensure that the work of the department is delivered as effectively and efficiently as possible. The administrator is often the first point of contact for patients and professionals contacting the service and plays an important role in ensuring a positive patient experience and positive image of the service. You will be proactive and organised and have experience as an administrator. You will be committed to providing a high-quality service and have a desire to work collaboratively with a range of colleagues. About the team: You will be part of the adult Neurodevelopmental Disorder services and work within Adult ADHD/ASD services. About the location: The team is based at Jubilee Health Centre, Wallington. Agile working is supported within the team The post will be working with the ADHD/ASD Services. Administrative tasks will include using computerised information systems (RiO), collating statistics and returns as required by the Trust, word-processing, audio typing, booking appointments and being the first point of contact for patients, families and professionals. To be responsible for ensuring the data on RIO is accurate and up to date. The post holder will extract routine data for the Trust and/or team members. To produce reports and alert team to errors and problems as they arise. To be responsible for providing monthly returns and other monthly performance indicators in a timely manner. To provide other returns as requested. To ensure that all patients and visitors are received in a courteous and efficient manner, covering reception when required. To be responsible for ensuring referrals to the team are processed efficiently. Responding to urgent referrals and queries when necessary and making sure they are passed on to a senior member of the team. To facilitate effective communication within the team by providing team members with messages and information. To ensure that all telephone and email enquiries to the team are handled politely and sympathetically, ensuring that all messages are passed on to the appropriate person in a timely and accurate manner which may often involve dealing with difficult and distressed patients on the phone or in person. To support the administration of multi-agency meetings, panels and forums as required to attend, including the preparation/distribution of agendas and associated papers, formal minute taking and follow up actions and distribute these as appropriate. To maintain confidentiality of service users and professional information at all times. Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in job applications If you have used AI to support the preparation of your application, please briefly indicate how it was used within your supporting statement or application form. Please remember, your application is your opportunity to tell us about your skills, experience and motivation for the role. We encourage applicants to complete their application and supporting statement in their own words wherever possible. We recognise that AI tools can be helpful in supporting accessibility, and for improving spelling, grammar and structure. Applications that rely heavily on AI-generated content can become generic and fail to accurately reflect an applicant's individual experience. Applications that clearly demonstrate your own voice, reflections and experiences are often the most effective and help us better understand your suitability for the role. Please be aware that information provided in your application and supporting statement may be explored further during the selection process. It is important that all applications accurately represent your own knowledge, skills and experience.

title: Administrator
description: We are looking to recruit an administrator to join our friendly team on a permanent contact, immediate start. The successful applicant will be required to work full time (37.5 hours), shifts between 8am and 8pm Monday and Tuesday to Friday 8am and 6.30pm. Applicants must be flexible and reliable. The purpose of the role is to: Assist with referral letters, hospital correspondence, workflow, scanning, call and recall and quarterly submission. To receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way. And to provide efficient, helpful, informative and supportive reception and administration services to patients and members of the primary health care team. Undertake a variety of administrative and clinical duties to assist in the smooth running of the practice including the provision of clerical support to clinical staff and other members of the Practice team Facilitate effective communication between patients, members of the primary health care team, secondary care and other associated healthcare agencies Specific delegated clinical tasks under the supervision of the GP Partners in accordance to practice guidelines Join our busy, forward-thinking GP practice as an Administration & Workflow Coordinator, where youll play a vital role in keeping patient care running safely, efficiently, and seamlessly behind the scenes. This is a dynamic position at the heart of the practice, managing clinical systems such as EMIS, Abtrace and AccuRx, coordinating referrals, processing medical reports, and ensuring all patient communications and records are handled accurately and in line with NHS and practice standards. You will work closely with clinicians, hospitals, and patients to support timely care, maintain workflows, and contribute to key areas such as Quality Outcomes Framework (QOF), audits, and risk management. The role also includes reception support, handling patient queries, and ensuring a high-quality, patient-focused service at all times. We are looking for someone organised, proactive, and detail-oriented, with strong communication skills and the ability to manage competing priorities. You should be confident using clinical systems, able to problem-solve independently, and comfortable working in a fast-paced healthcare environment. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who wants to make a real impact in primary care, develop their skills, and be part of a supportive team committed to delivering high-quality patient care. Duties and Responsibilities Duties and responsibilities may vary from time to time under the direction of the Business Practice Manager and Partners, depending on practice workload, staffing levels, and evolving service needs. All tasks must be carried out in accordance with practice policies, procedures, and relevant guidelines. Manage and maintain document workflow systems, ensuring timely and accurate processing of all incoming and outgoing clinical correspondence. Process referrals in the absence of the medical secretary, ensuring compliance with practice protocols and timely submission. Manage requests for medical reports, including insurance reports and copies of medical records, ensuring appropriate authorisation and turnaround times. Advise patients on applicable fees for private (non-GMS) services, process payments, and issue receipts in line with practice policy. Liaise with hospitals and external providers to ensure patients receive appropriate appointments and follow-ups. Monitor and manage workflow systems to ensure all tasks are completed within required timeframes. Maintain up-to-date scanning and document filing processes. Support call and recall systems to ensure patients are invited for relevant reviews, screenings, and follow-ups. Process and distribute incoming and outgoing mail efficiently. Process pathology results via electronic systems in accordance with practice protocols. Manage online requests, including patient queries and emails, ensuring timely and appropriate responses. Undertake accurate data entry, coding, and summarising of patient records in line with clinical standards. Respond to enquiries from patients, colleagues, healthcare professionals, and external organisations in a professional and timely manner. Provide general administrative support including document preparation, filing, photocopying, and scanning. Support delivery of the Quality Outcomes Framework (QOF) and other contractual requirements. Assist with audits, data collection, and risk management activities. Attend non-clinical meetings as required and provide accurate minute taking. Maintain and update the practice website as required. Report building or facilities issues in the absence of management. Provide first-line support for basic IT issues and escalate where necessary. Provide reception cover as required, including processing repeat prescriptions and ensuring prescriptions are ready within 48 hours where appropriate. Prepare clinical rooms for surgeries and ensure adequate stock of consumables. Deliver an efficient and patient-focused reception service. Handle general enquiries, explain procedures, and book appointments appropriately. Use judgement to prioritise and manage patients requiring urgent attention without disrupting service flow. Register new patients and temporary residents, ensuring all procedures are completed accurately. Manage telephone calls, including taking and relaying messages accurately and promptly. Record home visit requests clearly and escalate to the Duty Doctor where appropriate. Act on clinician requests for further information, ensuring all documentation and follow-up actions are completed. Support the review and updating of practice policies and procedures as required. Personal/Professional Development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work. Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources. Communication: The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognize peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly. Contribution to the Implementation of Services: The post-holder will: Apply practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate. The above list of duties is not exhaustive and may be subject to change as deemed necessary.

title: Receptionist/Administrator
description: Marylebone Health Centre is looking for a friendly, professional and organised Receptionist/Administrator to join our busy reception and administration team. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys working with people and wants to make a real difference in supporting patient care. As the first point of contact for patients and visitors, youll provide a warm and professional welcomewhether in person or over the phone. Youll support patients in accessing the right healthcare professional or service, while ensuring the smooth day-to-day running of the practice. Why Join Us? At Marylebone Health Centre, you'll be part of a supportive, patient-focused team that values professionalism, teamwork and high-quality care. We offer training and development opportunities, regular team meetings, and the chance to make a meaningful impact every day. How to Apply - Please send your CV & Application Formto CLCCG.PPG@nhs.net

title: Receptionist/ Administrator
description: Support clinicians in clinical administrate tasks such as correspondence management, referrals, communicating with hospitals and other external organisations. Signpost patients to the most appropriate service depending on their needs. Educate patients about the range of specialist services available locally and directing patients to the right care more quickly both inside and outside primary care. Work collaboratively with administrative and clinical colleagues to provide an efficient and effective service. Support patients and other healthcare professionals both in person and over the telephone, delivering a professional, friendly, and helpful service at all times. Manage day-to-day administrative tasks and prioritise workload effectively to ensure the smooth running of the practice. Reception greeting patients in a friendly manner show patients how to use check in screens handling repeat prescription requests and collections consulting with members of the practice team about waiting area (delays etc) Telephone triage /appointments have working knowledge of telephone system, during and after hours fill in the telephone triage template triaging and booking into appropriate appointments with clinicians signposting patients to relevant services both internally and externally Administration To have thorough knowledge of all practice procedures and policies Scanning and processing clinical correspondence Tasks (contacting hospitals, calling patients, booking transport etc) Creating and processing referrals Register patients Processing links Check emails Processing medical records in and out Dealing with medical record/report requests Patient support Help reduce demand by working on a list of high service users to help and support them by contacting them on a regular basis instead of them contacting us. Other tasks Room/stock checks Opening/ closing the practice Any other tasks allocated by managers

title: Administrator
description: We have a great opportunity to join our surgeryas an Administrator . We are looking for an enthusiastic & organised individual with a positive, can-do attitude to join our excellent admin team. Ideally, you will have experience of managing childhood immunisation programmes and new patient registrations, alongside general practice administration.The role is 16 hours per week over 4 days, working 4 hours per day . Working times can be arranged around school runs, making this an ideal opportunity for someone looking for part-time hours. The role includes a varied range of responsibilities, including: Childhood Immunisations: Ensure that all patients aged 5 years and under are appropriately invited for their childhood immunisations and that immunisation records and schedules are accurately maintained and kept up to date. New Patient Registrations Undertake the administrative and clerical processes associated with new patient registrations, including processing electronic and paper registration forms accurately and promptly. Liaise with colleagues and relevant external organisations as required. General Administration Provide administrative support across other areas of the practice, contributing to the effective day-to-day running of the service. The successful candidate will be organised, reliable and able to work effectively as part of a busy team, with excellent attention to detail and a commitment to delivering a high-quality service. The following are the core responsibilities of the Administrator . On occasion, there may be a requirement to undertake additional duties, depending on factors such as workload and staffing levels: Childhood Immunisations: Manage the administrative processes relating to childhood immunisations, ensuring invitations, records and schedules are accurate and kept up to date. New Patient Registrations: Manage the administrative processes associated with new patient registrations, ensuring registrations are processed accurately and promptly. General Administration: Undertake other administrative duties as required, including taking minutes at practice and team meetings and assisting other members of the administrative team. The following are the core responsibilities of the Administrator. There may be on occasion, a requirement to carry out other tasks; this will be dependent upon factors such as workload and staffing levels: Childhood immunisations and registration Registering new-born babies Arranging baby health checks appointment with a doctor and first immunisation appointment with nurse (appointments must be given at 8 weeks of age, in line with public health targets) Book all babies for their immunisations and follow up on those who DNA. Search and recalling patients for immunisations weekly-monthly. Nominated administrative person, responsible for contacting Health Visitors re patients who DNR-DNA. Review immunisation status for new patients registering with the practice and recall if required. Investigating weekly immunisation list from Child Health. Liaising with nurses regarding catch up campaigns and co-ordinating the campaign as and when required. Liaise with HV regarding registration and deregistration of Under5s - Under16. New Patient Registrations Process and register new patients accurately and in a timely manner, including both electronic and paper registrations. Liaise with PCSE regarding patient registrations and maintain registration links and associated information on the clinical system. Accurately record relevant information for newly registered patients, including ethnicity and main spoken language. Process changes to patient demographic information, including names and addresses. Explain practice arrangements and registration requirements to new patients and patients requesting temporary registration. Ensure all required registration procedures and documentation are completed accurately. Deal with telephone and other enquiries relating to patient registrations, taking messages or referring queries to the appropriate team member where necessary. Enter and update patient information on the clinical system as required. Ensure regular and temporary patients are registered on the clinical system promptly and accurately. Liaise with colleagues and relevant external organisations regarding registration queries, in accordance with practice policies and procedures. Other administration tasks To assist other administration roles covering sickness and annual leave. Assist with any other reasonable requests by the management or partners. Attend Clinical meetings and take accurate minutes. Attend Open Business meeting and take accurate minutes. Attend Nurses meeting and take accurate minutes.

title: Receptionist
description: Come and join our friendly team at St Mary Cray Practice. We are looking for an enthusiastic and caring Receptionist who can provide a helpful and professional service to our patients while supporting the smooth running of the practice. This would suit someone with excellent communication and organisational skills who enjoys working with people and being part of a busy team. GP practice experience is desirable but not essential, as support and training will be provided. The receptionist will provide a friendly, professional and efficient service to patients and support the day-to-day running of the GP practice. Main duties include: Welcoming patients and visitors and dealing with enquiries appropriately. Answering telephone calls and directing queries to the appropriate person or service. Booking, cancelling and rearranging appointments. Helping patients access the most appropriate healthcare service. Processing prescription, referral, test result and general patient enquiries. Registering new patients and updating patient details. Maintaining accurate patient records on the clinical system. Scanning and processing correspondence and clinical documents. Providing administrative support to GPs, nurses and the wider practice team. Liaising with hospitals, pharmacies and other NHS services. Dealing sensitively with patients who may be anxious, upset or frustrated. Maintaining confidentiality and following data protection procedures. Working closely with the reception and administration team to provide an efficient service. Undertaking other reasonable duties to support the smooth running of the practice. Main duties of the job for a Part-time receptionist Hours to be 10 - 15 hours per week.

title: Receptionist
description: Blackheath Standard PMS are looking for an experienced and reliable receptionist to join our friendly Reception Team. The practice is situated in a pleasant part of Blackheath in South East London with good transport links and local shops. The position is for 22 hours per week over four days, based on a seven week rolling rota. Please note that the rota is variable and you will be working different days over a seven week period. This is based on a 7am start and 12.30pm finish 8am start and 1pm finish, 1pm start and 6pm finish, 1.30pm start with a 7pm finish.
