Saturday mornings are part of our enhanced access service and there is the option to work these sessions on a rotation basis. We are a friendly team, who are supportive of each other and there will be opportunity to develop new skills. Duties include: Covering reception desk, answering telephone calls, booking appointments via AccuRx triage system, dealing with patient queries, order prescriptions, process admin duties for clinical staff, general administration such as filing and liaising with other health care providers in a professional manner, and processing clinical letters through the Docman system. The duties are variable, depending on what is required on the day. Candidates must have strong communication skills, be friendly, reliable and willing to learn. The applicant must have the ability to prioritise workload. Applicants must have the ability to work within a team, have experience of EMIS, AccuRx and Docman and IT skills. Previous experience of working in General Practice is essential, further training will be available for any candidates that show a passion for learning. Job Description Main duties include: Covering reception desk greeting patients and visitors with a professional and friendly manner. Manage the booking system efficiently, signposting patients to the relevant services. Answering incoming calls, respond to queries and manage email correspondence promptly. Assist clinicians as needed, including handling paperwork, stocking consultation rooms and daily end of day duties to ensure the rooms are meeting infection control standards. Manage office supplies, handling incoming/outgoing post and perform general administrative duties. Maintain accurate patient records and ensure confidentiality. Candidates must have strong communication skills, be friendly, reliable and willing to learn and develop their skills.In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice Health & Safety Policy. The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues. The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment. The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise needs of people for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly.

title: Receptionist / Administrator [PART TIME]
description: We are seeking a friendly and organised Receptionist / Administrator to join our team on a part time basis . We are looking for someone to work between 15 - 20 hours per week, over the course of the week. The timings and exact days will be discussed during the interview process. We can be flexible, within reason. The hours will be a mixture of morning shifts, starting at 8am and evening shifts finishing at 6:30pm, including the occasional Saturday shifts once the candidate is fully trained. We would ideally like the candidate to have experience working with the clinical system, SystmOne however this is not essential. We also use PATCHS and AccuRx so experience with this would be great. It is essential that you have experience of working with the public, customer service or patient facing type role. Full training will be provided either way. Experience of working within a GP practice is not essential. The practice is open Monday - Friday 08:00 - 18:30 & Saturday's 09:00 - 12:00. Provide a friendly and efficient first point of contact for patients and visitors, handling enquiries in person and by telephone and directing patients to the appropriate clinician or service. Manage appointment bookings and the flow of patients, record relevant information, and explain practice arrangements and registration requirements. Process new patient registrations, repeat prescription requests and patient correspondence; update records and scan documents into the clinical system. Use the appointment and telephone systems, take messages and ensure calls are routed appropriately. Keep reception and waiting areas tidy, maintain strict confidentiality, follow practice procedures, and support colleagues with cover and other delegated administrative duties. Ensure an effective, efficient and responsive reception service is provided to patients and all other visitors to the practice, including monitoring flow of patients into consulting and treatment rooms Deal with general enquiries, both over the telephone and in person, in a courteous manner and explain procedures where necessary. Take and disseminate messages when required. To deal with difficult patients, in reception and on the phone, in a calm manner and seek management support as and when required. Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way. Explain practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover. Ensure necessary procedures are completed. Produce repeat prescriptions according to practice procedures and ensure timely distribution of completed prescriptions. Advice patients of relevant charges for private services, accept payment and issue receipts for the same. Ensure reception and waiting areas are kept neat and tidy. Receive and accurately record requests for home visits, assessing urgency in accordance with the Practice protocol. Re-stock practice rooms and re-order as appropriate. Participate in proactive forward planning identifying and implanting improvements within and beyond key result areas. To deal with complaints from the patients and other visitors and deal with them in line with the practice policy and procedures. Assist with the production of general letters and reports, medical insurance reports, letters and referrals for professional staff as and when required. Management of Appointment Systems and medical records Ensure total familiarity with appointment systems through training and self-assessment on System One. To signpost patients to the most appropriate healthcare professional i.e. ANT, HCA, Nurse and/or GPS. Book appointments ensuring sufficient information is recorded to retrieve medical and computer record and to identify the purpose of the appointment. To support other healthcare professionals with patient recall, as and when required. Monitor effectiveness of the system and report any problems. Retrieve and re-file records as required ensuring that strict alphabetical order is followed. title: Receptionist

The role is essential in ensuring the smooth and efficient running of the practice on a daily basis. You will provide a professional, caring, and confidential reception and administrative service, supporting both patients and the clinical team. This includes managing appointments, handling telephone and face-to-face enquiries, processing prescriptions, and maintaining accurate patient records using clinical systems such as EMIS Web. You will play an important part in ensuring patients are directed to the right services and receive timely, appropriate care. Overall, the GP Receptionist role is vital in supporting high-quality patient care and contributing to the effective running of the NHS GP practice. Deal with patient queries in a calm and professional manner, including difficult or distressed individuals Ensure compliance with GDPR, NHS policies, and practice procedures Work effectively as part of a team in a busy, fast-paced primary care environment Job responsibilities Patient Services Act as the first point of contact for patients in person and by telephone Deal with patient enquiries in a polite, professional, and sensitive manner Book, cancel, and amend appointments accurately and efficiently Signpost patients to appropriate clinicians or services Assist with recall of patients needing annual or monitoring reviews Administration Duties Maintain accurate and up-to-date patient records using clinical systems Process repeat prescription requests following practice protocols Scan, file, and manage incoming and outgoing correspondence Support administrative tasks including referrals and clinical document processing Processing patient registrations Team Support Work closely with GPs, nurses, and the wider practice team Assist with the organisation of clinics and daily workflows Support colleagues to ensure smooth and efficient service delivery Confidentiality & Compliance Maintain strict confidentiality in line with GDPR and NHS policies Follow all practice procedures, protocols, and safeguarding requirements Ensure a professional and safe reception environment at all times General Responsibilities Manage a busy workload in a fast-paced environment Remain calm and professional when dealing with difficult or distressed patients Work effectively as part of a team and support colleagues when required Participate in training and continuous development relevant to the role

description: Medical Receptionist GP Practice Working days/hours: Monday -14.00pm - 18.30pm Wednesday - 14.00pm - 18.30pm Thursday - 13.00pm - 18.00pm Friday -14.00pm - 18.30pm We are looking for a friendly, organised and enthusiastic Medical Receptionist to join our busy GP Practice team. Telephone and Communication Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and professionally, directing enquiries to the appropriate person or department. Administrative Duties Undertake a range of general administrative duties to support the efficient operation of the Practice. Retrieve, organise and re-file paper medical records where required, ensuring appropriate filing procedures are followed. Ensure patient records and documentation are maintained in good condition and stored securely. Accept payments, issue receipts and maintain accurate records of transactions in accordance with Practice procedures. 6. Teamwork and General Responsibilities Work collaboratively with GPs, nurses, administrative colleagues and the wider Practice team to ensure a high standard of patient service. Support colleagues during busy periods and contribute to the effective day-to-day running of the Practice. Follow all Practice policies and procedures, including safeguarding, health and safety, infection prevention and control, and confidentiality. Attend relevant training, staff meetings and development activities as required. The successful candidate will be expected to provide cover for thier colleagues during periods of annual leave and sick leave, subject to operational requirements. Undertake any other reasonable duties appropriate to the role, as directed by the Practice Manager or the Partners.

description: Earl's Court Medical Centre has an exciting opportunity for a Medical Receptionist to join our welcoming and forward thinking Practice team on a part-time basis. Your normal pattern of working will be Monday - Friday, within the hours of 8am-6:30pm (5 hours per day). Interested applicants must have primary care and SystmOne experience. Key Responsibilities include: Greeting and assisting patients at the reception desk Managing appointments, cancellations and patients enquiries Answering telephone calls and directing queries appropriately Processing repeat prescription requests Supporting the administrative and clinical team with day-to-day tasks Maintaining confidentially and ensuring accurate record- keeping Processing ingoing and outgoing patient records This is a patient facing role that requires excellent communication skills, attention to detail, and a calm, efficient approach to working in a fast-paced environment. Reception duties: Ensure an effective and efficient reception service is provided to patients and any other visitors to the Practice. Deal with all general enquiries, explain procedures and make new and follow-up appointments. Using your own judgment and communication skills ensure that patients with no prior appointment but who need urgent consultation are seen in a logical and non-disruptive manner. Explain Practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover and ensure procedures are completed. Receive and make telephone calls as required. Personal/Professional Development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the Practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of their own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for their own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Quality : The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the Practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication : The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the Implementation of Services: The post-holder will: Apply Practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate

title: Receptionist
description: Blackheath Standard PMS are looking for an experienced and reliable receptionist to join our friendly Reception Team. The practice is situated in a pleasant part of Blackheath in South East London with good transport links and local shops. The position is for 22 hours per week over four days, based on a seven week rolling rota. Please note that the rota is variable and you will be working different days over a seven week period. This is based on a 7am start and 12.30pm finish 8am start and 1pm finish, 1pm start and 6pm finish, 1.30pm start with a 7pm finish. This can vary , depending on the needs of the practice during sickness and annual leave. Flexibility is essential. Saturday mornings are part of our enhanced access service and there is the option to work these sessions on a rotation basis. We are a friendly team, who are supportive of each other and there will be opportunity to develop new skills. Duties include: Covering reception desk, answering telephone calls, booking appointments via AccuRx triage system, dealing with patient queries, order prescriptions, process admin duties for clinical staff, general administration such as filing and liaising with other health care providers in a professional manner, and processing clinical letters through the Docman system. The duties are variable, depending on what is required on the day. Candidates must have strong communication skills, be friendly, reliable and willing to learn. The applicant must have the ability to prioritise workload. Applicants must have the ability to work within a team, have experience of EMIS, AccuRx and Docman and IT skills. Previous experience of working in General Practice is essential, further training will be available for any candidates that show a passion for learning. Job Description Main duties include: Covering reception desk greeting patients and visitors with a professional and friendly manner. Manage the booking system efficiently, signposting patients to the relevant services. Answering incoming calls, respond to queries and manage email correspondence promptly. Assist clinicians as needed, including handling paperwork, stocking consultation rooms and daily end of day duties to ensure the rooms are meeting infection control standards. Manage office supplies, handling incoming/outgoing post and perform general administrative duties. Maintain accurate patient records and ensure confidentiality. Candidates must have strong communication skills, be friendly, reliable and willing to learn and develop their skills.In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice Health & Safety Policy. The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues. The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment. The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise needs of people for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly.

description: This position is five day a week (Mon to Fri) on site with no remote working. The trust does not offer visa sponsorship for this post. Tyson West 1 is part of Bethlem Royal Hospital. We offer services for men, aged 18-65, who have acute mental illness and require 24 hour hospital care. Acute illnesses start quickly and have distressing symptoms.We provide care for people who live in the London Borough of Croydon.We offer psychiatric assessment, care and treatment in hospital, which helps to reduce the risk to self and others.Our service brings together teams of health and social care professionals, including nurses, psychologists, OTs, social workers and psychiatrists. This position is five day a week on site with no remote working. We are looking for a highly organised, efficient, flexible and proactive person with excellent communication skills to work in the busy post, and who can balance work demands along with the changing needs of the service. The role requires the post holder to communicate with patients, ward staff and visitors, and to develop collaborative working relationships with colleagues and external agencies. The post holder must have an excellent telephone manner, good IT skills with experience using Microsoft Office packages (Work, Excel and Outlook) . To monitor supplies of patient information such as welcome packs.Administration:To assist in providing a comprehensive administrative service to the multi-disciplinary teams, which include but not limited to data inputting patient information, scanning documents and uploading to patient database. Maintaining efficient and effective administration systems to support the needs of the service, working with other members of the admin team as appropriate to achieve this. title: Patient Services Advisor/receptionist
description: Are you an experienced Receptionist/Administrative assistant or someone with transferrable skills who is good with people and can balance a varying workload? The Reception teams across Groves Health are the lynchpin of our business and support the Group to provide a first class service to our patients and the wider community. The role:- This is a varied role which will give you the opportunity to have exposure to different parts of Reception/Administration on a rotating basis within a busy GP surgery. Some of your duties will include:- Booking telephone appointments with patients Managing the incoming email inbox and patient requests Responding to patient queries via the Practice website dashboard Greeting patients when they arrive in the Practice and dealing with queries Calling patients on behalf of GP's to book appointments and relay information Managing incoming mail and distributing/scanning accordingly On occasion opening and closing the Practice Working with outside agencies such as Pharmacies and Care homes for patient care Registering new patients Using Practice software such as EMIS, Docman (training provided) and Office products Groves Health is a successful and trusted provider of NHS services across England. Over the past five years, we have grown from a single practice in New Malden to a team of more than 100 people, providing high-quality care to patients and communities across our four sites in New Malden, Richmond, Wimbledon and Hinchley Wood. As Groves Health continues to grow and expand the services we provide, we are looking for an enthusiastic and reliable Receptionist & Administrator to join our team at Groves New Malden. We are looking for someone who enjoys working with people, is well organised and can manage a varied workload in a busy environment. Previous experience in a GP practice, healthcare or administrative setting would be beneficial, but we are also keen to hear from candidates with transferable skills and a strong commitment to providing excellent customer service. Our Reception teams play a vital role in the day-to-day running of our practices. As one of the first points of contact for patients, you will help ensure that patients receive a friendly, professional and efficient service. This is a varied role, providing the opportunity to develop your knowledge and experience across different areas of reception and administration within a busy GP surgery. Your duties will include, but are not limited to: Booking and managing telephone appointments for patients. Managing the practice email inbox and responding to patient requests. Responding to patient queries through the practice website and online services. Welcoming patients to the practice and dealing with their queries in a professional and helpful manner. Contacting patients on behalf of GPs and other members of the clinical team to arrange appointments or relay information. Receiving, sorting, scanning and distributing incoming post and correspondence. Registering new patients and ensuring their information is accurately recorded. Liaising with external organisations, including pharmacies, care homes and other healthcare services, where appropriate to support patient care. Using practice and administrative systems, including EMIS, Docman and Microsoft Office . Full training will be provided where required. Supporting colleagues with general administrative duties and contributing to the smooth running of the practice. Assisting with the opening and closing of the practice when required. We are looking for someone who: Has excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Is friendly, approachable and professional. Has a strong commitment to providing excellent patient service. Is organised and able to prioritise competing demands. Can remain calm and professional when working in a busy environment. Has good attention to detail and is confident using computer systems. Is able to work effectively both independently and as part of a team. Is adaptable and willing to learn new systems and processes. Understands the importance of confidentiality and handling patient information appropriately. Previous experience within a GP practice, NHS or healthcare environment would be advantageous, but is not essential. This is an excellent opportunity to join a growing organisation where you will be part of a supportive team and have the opportunity to develop your skills and experience within primary care. If you are enthusiastic, organised and passionate about providing a high-quality service to patients, we would love to hear from you.

title: GP Receptionist
description: This is a part-time receptionist role for 20 hours a week. The post holder is responsible for the smooth and effective running of the GP Front Office Desk by providing an efficient, professional and welcoming reception and administrative service to patients, clinicians and visitors. The post holder will be the first point of contact for patients and will undertake a range of reception, clerical and administrative duties to ensure that patient enquiries, appointments, and correspondence and administrative tasks are managed accurately and efficiently. The role requires excellent communication, organisational and customer service skills, together with the ability to work under pressure, maintain confidentially and work collaboratively as part of the wider practice team. Appointment Management Book, amend and cancel appointments in accordance with practice procedure. Direct patients to the appropriate clinician or service in accordance with the agreed care navigation protocols. Escalate urgent clinician concerns to the appropriate clinician without delay. Manage appointment cancellations and rearrangements Telephone and Communication Duties Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and professionally as and when needed Identify urgent calls and follow the practice's escalation procedures General Administrative Duties Update patient demographics details, including addresses, telephone numbers and contact information. Scan, upload, index and file incoming correspondence Register new patients and process patient registration documentation if needed Prescription Administration Receive and process repeat prescription request in accordance with the practice procedures Deal with general prescription collection and processing enquiries Forward prescription request to the appropriate workflow or authorised clinical team Practice Support & Organisation Assist with the day-to-day organisation of reception and administrative services and tasks. Informoperations manager for any adequate supplies of stationary forms and patient information leaflets Assist with the opening and closing procedures when required Support colleague during busy periods and staff absences Participate in practice meetings, training and service improvement activities Key Responsibilities A. Reception and Patient Services Welcome patients and visitors in a friendly, professional and courteous manner. Act as the first point of contact for patients attending the surgery. Assist patients in for appointments and update their attendance status on the clinical system. Deal with face-to-face, telephone and online enquiries efficiently and sensitively. Provide and signpost patients for general information about practice services, opening hours and appointment procedures. Assist patients with queries and direct them to the appropriate healthcare professional or department. Maintain a professional and welcoming reception environment. Deal with difficult or challenging situations calmly and escalate concerns appropriately. Support patients who may be vulnerable, distressed or require additional assistance. B. Appointment Management Book, amend and cancel appointments in accordance with practice procedures. Manage appointment requests by telephone, online and face-to-face. Direct patients to the appropriate clinician or service in accordance with agreed care navigation protocols. Monitor appointment availability and follow booking guidelines. Manage appointment cancellations and rearrangements. Inform patients of appointment changes where required. Escalate urgent clinical concerns to the appropriate clinician without delay. C. Telephone and Communication Duties Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and professionally as and when needed. Take accurate messages from Clinics, Hospital, Emergency Service Team, Other GP Surgeries and ensure they are passed to the relevant staff member. Transfer calls to GPs, nurses, management or other departments as appropriate. Identify urgent calls and follow the practice's escalation procedures. Communicate professionally with hospitals, pharmacies, community services and other healthcare providers. D. General Administrative Duties Register new patients and process patient registration documentation. Update patient demographic details, including addresses, telephone numbers and contact information. Scan, upload, index and file incoming correspondence. Process incoming and outgoing post. Maintain accurate electronic and paper-based records. Process requests for medical records and documentation in line with practice policies. Prepare, photocopy and distribute documents as required. Handle general administrative correspondence and enquiries. Assist with the preparation of reports, spreadsheets and other administrative documents. Maintain filing systems and ensure documents are stored appropriately. Support the Practice Manager and wider administrative team with day-to-day tasks. F. Prescription Administration Receive and process repeat prescription requests in accordance with practice procedures. Forward prescription requests to the appropriate workflow or authorised clinical team. Deal with general prescription collection and processing enquiries. Liaise with community pharmacies regarding administrative prescription queries. Direct medication-related clinical questions to an appropriate clinician. Maintain confidentiality when handling prescription requests. H. Practice Support and Organisation Assist with the day-to-day organisation of reception and administrative services. Inform Operations Manager for any adequate supplies of stationery, forms and patient information leaflets. Ensure the reception and waiting areas are tidy, organised and welcoming. Report equipment faults, maintenance issues and health and safety concerns. Assist with opening and closing procedures where required. Support colleagues during busy periods and staff absences. Participate in practice meetings, training and service improvement activities. I. Confidentiality and Information Governance Maintain strict patient confidentiality at all times. Comply with GDPR, Data Protection Act 2018 and NHS information governance requirements. Ensure patient information is only accessed and shared where there is an appropriate reason and authorisation. Verify patient identity before disclosing confidential information. Ensure computer systems and patient records are protected from unauthorised access. Follow practice policies relating to information security and confidentiality. Report any actual or suspected data breaches promptly. This list is not exhaustive and the post holder will be expected to carry out any other reasonable requests as instructed by the line manager.

title: GP Receptionist
description: The Receptionist is primarily responsible for undertaking a wide range of reception duties and the provision of general support to the wider multi-professional team. A sound professional working relationship will be required with the GPs and staff working within the Practice. We are expanding the reception team and the role requires high levels of organisation and excellent interpersonal skills. The post requires excellent communication skills, high levels of organisation and attention to detail as well as the ability to exercise tact, discretion and initiative. The ability to work under pressure and as part of a team are equally important. The Practice will support continuing education and professional development in the form of attendance at study days, courses and with in-house training, as deemed appropriate for the benefit of both the individual and the Practice. Open up surgery, switching on clinicians PCs and ensuring everything is set up for the day. Ensure building security, have thorough knowledge of doors, windows and alarms. Keep reception and waiting rooms areas tidy. Booking appointments face to face and over the phone and signposting to ensure the patient is booked with the right person, in the right place at the right time. Checking patients in for appointments and directing to appropriate waiting area. Receiving and recording requests for home visits, DN visits, telephone consultations and taking messages. Giving normal test results to patients or chasing up when necessary. Access incoming emails via generic inbox , online consultations and web contacts signposting and taking all the appropriate action. Completing patient registrations and adding details on to the computer when necessary. Data input of new patient questionnaires. Supporting GP Links processes such as preparing notes for sending off, filing incoming notes and ensuring filed medical records are accurately stored. Process patients change of address, numbers, etc. Process prescription requests in accordance with practice guidelines including filing prescriptions and recording in pharmacy book. Handing completed repeat prescriptions to patients, checking name and address. Receiving and recording payments for medicals, insurance reports, etc General administrative tasks. Making sure there is good supply of, and printing when necessary, practice leaflets, new patient questionnaires, change of address forms etc Monitoring the clinics and letting patients know when delays and clinicians when late visits, etc added. Completing DN referrals and emailing to referral centre. Helping to assist with general enquiries. Answer incoming calls in a timely manner as per practice protocol. Be able to cover all care navigator roles as required including extended hour surgeries. Have knowledge of and work in accordance with practice policies and procedures. Pulling/filing notes as necessary. Scan and photocopy as required. Ensure post and clinical forms are correctly filed and waiting for collection. Ensuring accurate recording of information using the practice clinical systems. Ensuring effective handover of matters outstanding to the incoming receptionists at end of shift. Make sure post tray is cleared every evening. Complete team EMIS & DOCMAN tasks. Contacting patients on the doctors behalf to arrange follow up appointments, prescription collections, test results etc Ordering ambulances as and when required by the clinician. Chaperone for clinicians. Greeting visitors and asking them to sign the visitors book, informing appropriate managers/colleagues of their presence. Taking deliveries or directing to relevant department Any other duties commensurate with the role. The above list of duties is not exhaustive and may be subject to change as deemed necessary

This frontline position is often the first point of contact for patients, providing a welcoming and professional service both in person and over the phone. The role combines traditional reception duties with care navigation, helping patients access the right care at the right time. This includes managing appointments, handling enquiries, signposting patients to appropriate services, and supporting clinical teams in the smooth running of the practice. Greeting and assisting patients in a friendly and professional manner. Managing patient appointments, cancellations, and repeat prescriptions. Handling telephone and face-to-face enquiries with empathy and confidentiality. Navigating patients to the most appropriate healthcare professional or community service. Supporting clinicians with administrative tasks to improve patient flow and access. Maintaining accurate records and updating patient information in line with data protection standards. Working collaboratively as part of the practice team to ensure a high standard of care. This role requires excellent communication skills, strong organisational abilities, and a patient-centred approach. The GP Surgery Receptionist / Care Navigator is instrumental in enhancing patient experience and supporting the delivery of primary care services. The GP Surgery Receptionist/Care Navigator is the first point of contact for patients and visitors, providing a professional, efficient, and friendly service. The role combines reception duties with care navigation, helping patients access the most appropriate care and services in a timely manner. The post-holder will contribute to the smooth running of the practice by managing patient enquiries, supporting clinicians, and ensuring excellent communication across the practice team. Key Responsibilities: Reception Duties: Welcome patients and visitors in a professional and caring manner Manage telephone calls, emails, and face-to-face enquiries promptly and efficiently Book, amend, and cancel patient appointments using the clinical system Process repeat prescription requests in line with practice protocols Process incoming and outgoing correspondence in line with practice protocol

title: Medical Receptionist
description: We are looking to recruit an exceptional Medical Receptionist to complement our existing team. The hours are full-time or part-time across 4 day s: a minimum of 30 and a maximum of 37.5 hrs / week . Mondays and Fridays are essential (unfortunately, we cannot offer flexibility on this). We offer competitive rates of pay, a large, friendly team, modern, purpose-built premises, an NHS Pension, and a free annual flu jab. This role would suit someone who is looking for an opportunity to develop their existing customer service skills in a fast-paced progressive environment. The ideal candidate will have excellent verbal and written communication skills. They will be empathetic, compassionate, patient focused and driven to provide exacting standards of care. We require someone who is resilient, adaptable to change, positive, enthusiastic, and an effective team player. Experience in EMIS Web and Docman is desirable but not essential. The purpose of this role is to deliver a high level of customer care to patients. The receptionists are front-line and should promote a professional and friendly image to patients and visitors at all times. They also provide an essential support function to the clinical and management teams. Dealing with enquiries from patients, internal personnel and external organisations in a professional and efficient manner. Receiving and directing patients and visitors on arrival at the practice with courtesy. Dealing with Anima requests in a friendly professional manner, ensuring confidentiality according to the practice procedure. Handling all telephone enquiries and requests within the practice telephone protocol. Operating the clinical system to book, cancel and amend appointments. Operating the clinical system to input and retrieve data as required. Responsible for receiving and recording messages efficiently and accurately according to practice procedure, ensuring that messages are conveyed to the clinical team in a timely manner. Liaising with the doctors regarding requests for home visits. Booking home visits as per practice protocol. Arranging interpreting services as and when required. Ensuring that all patient registration procedures are carried out accurately and that patients complete the necessary documentation. Ensuring that patient records are up to date and that information recorded is accurate and relevant. Dealing with patient tasks and requests on Anima and Emis tasks according to practice procedure. Managing outgoing mail as appropriate. Photocopying information when necessary. Responsible for handover at change of shift those outstanding queries and messages. Assisting with the resolution of patient complaints informally wherever possible. Escalating complaints to the Reception Managers or Complaints Manager as appropriate. Ensuring that the practice complaints leaflet is available to patients upon request. Ensuring the reception and waiting areas are kept clean, safe and tidy at all times. Responsibility for opening up and closing down the building as per practice procedure. Ensure till takings are accurately documented according to practice procedure. Attending any necessary training/ courses. Understanding and participating in annual appraisal and review. To be aware of the practice Health and Safety policies and ensure that correct and safe procedures are followed. To observe the rule of patient confidentiality and be aware of the Data Protection Act.

title: Receptionist / Care Navigator
description: The Ridgeway Surgery in Harrow is looking for a Care Navigator to help patients access the right care and make their experience of contacting the practice as straightforward as possible. Working closely with our clinical teams, you will review patient requests, coordinate appointments and follow-up, and guide patients towards appropriate services. You will use agreed practice pathways, with support from the duty clinician whenever advice is needed. You will also support core reception services when required, including the front desk, telephone calls and patient registrations. This is an opportunity to develop your skills in general practice and make a difference to patients every day. We offer structured training, shadowing and supervised practice, with your responsibilities developing as your confidence and experience grow. We are looking for someone who communicates clearly, listens carefully and remains calm under pressure. If you enjoy helping people, work well in a team and are keen to learn, we would welcome your application. Your main focus will be helping patients reach the most appropriate care through our online consultation system, telephone and face-to-face contact. You will clarify requests, check relevant information and use practice pathways to arrange appointments or direct patients to other services. You will work closely with the duty clinician, promptly escalating urgent concerns, safeguarding issues and any requests that need clinical judgement. You will help maintain continuity of care and support patients who need additional assistance to access services. Day-to-day work will also include coordinating routine reviews and follow-up, handling administrative queries and keeping accurate records. When required, you will support reception by welcoming patients at the front desk, answering calls, processing registrations and assisting with general enquiries. Job title: Care Navigator Employer: The Ridgeway Surgery, Harrow Location: Main surgery and Alexandra Avenue Health and Social Care Centre Accountable to: Reception Manager Clinical support: Duty clinician and wider clinical team To help patients access the most appropriate care, professional or service by reviewing requests, gathering relevant information and following agreed practice pathways. The Care Navigator will work closely with the clinical team to coordinate appointments and follow-up, support continuity of care and assist patients who need additional help accessing services. The postholder will also support core reception services when required. This is a non-clinical role. The postholder will work within their training and agreed procedures, seeking clinical advice whenever a request is unclear, raises concerns or requires clinical judgement. Review patient requests received through the practices online consultation system, by telephone and in person. Read the full request and check relevant information in the patient record, including previous consultations, existing plans and outstanding appointments. Contact patients to clarify requests or obtain further information, using agreed questions and procedures. Follow practice pathways to direct requests to the appropriate clinician, appointment type or service. Arrange appointments according to agreed priorities and clinical instructions. Support continuity of care by arranging follow-up with the same clinician where appropriate. Signpost patients to suitable services, including community pharmacies, community healthcare, social prescribing and voluntary sector support. Explain the next steps clearly and check that patients understand the arrangements. Recognise when a patient needs additional support to access care and help them use alternative routes where appropriate. Recognise urgent concerns and warning signs identified within practice training and pathways, and promptly alert the duty clinician. Escalate safeguarding concerns and requests involving vulnerable patients in accordance with practice procedures. Seek advice whenever information is incomplete, a pathway does not clearly apply or there is uncertainty about the appropriate action. Refer requests requiring diagnosis, treatment decisions or clinical interpretation to an appropriate clinician. Follow clinical instructions accurately and record the action taken. Work within the limits of the role and the postholders assessed competence. Follow practice procedures for emergencies and situations requiring immediate assistance. Help arrange long-term condition reviews, blood tests, vaccinations, screening and other planned care in accordance with practice pathways and documented clinical plans. Check whether relevant appointments, investigations or follow-up arrangements are already in place before making further bookings. Coordinate linked appointments where required, such as a blood test followed by a clinical review. Identify outstanding routine care recorded in the patients notes and bring this to the attention of the appropriate team. Support reminders, recalls and follow-up arrangements as directed. Liaise with clinicians and administrative colleagues to help resolve outstanding requests and avoid unnecessary duplication. Handle requests concerning prescriptions, fit notes, referrals, forms and other administrative matters using agreed procedures. Route medication requests and queries to the appropriate prescribing or clinical team, recognising when urgent escalation is needed. Check available referral information and provide patients with appropriate updates or contact details. Liaise with the administrative team where a referral or other enquiry requires further investigation. Keep patients informed about the progress of their requests within the information available and the limits of the role. Record communications and actions clearly so that colleagues can understand what has been done and what remains outstanding. Support core reception services when required, including front desk cover, telephone calls and patient registrations. Welcome patients and visitors, respond to enquiries and direct them to the appropriate colleague or service. Book, amend and cancel appointments in accordance with practice procedures. Process patient registrations and update demographic and contact details accurately. Take and pass on messages promptly, ensuring that urgent matters reach the appropriate person. Assist with routine reception administration and help maintain an organised reception area. Handle difficult conversations calmly and respectfully, seeking support when needed. Treat patients, carers and colleagues with courtesy, dignity and respect. Communicate clearly and sensitively, adapting communication to individual needs. Support patients who have difficulty using digital systems or who face language, communication or accessibility barriers. Arrange interpreting or other communication support in accordance with practice procedures. Maintain appropriate professional boundaries and protect privacy during conversations. Respond constructively to concerns and pass complaints to the appropriate colleague. Help ensure patients receive consistent information about accessing practice services. Maintain accurate, timely records of patient requests, communications and actions. Use clinical and administrative systems in accordance with training and practice policies. Access patient information only where needed to carry out the role. Maintain confidentiality and handle personal information securely. Follow identity verification procedures before disclosing information or changing patient details. Report information security incidents, errors or concerns promptly through the appropriate practice process. Work collaboratively with the clinical, care navigation, reception and administrative teams. Participate in induction, structured training, shadowing and supervised practice. Complete competency assessments and take on additional care navigation responsibilities as agreed following training. Attend relevant team meetings and keep up to date with changes to practice pathways and services. Share feedback about recurring problems and suggest improvements to patient access and administrative processes. Provide reasonable cover for colleagues within the postholders training and competence. Complete mandatory training and participate in appraisal and development discussions. The postholder must follow practice policies relating to safeguarding, equality and diversity, infection prevention, health and safety, confidentiality and professional conduct. The postholder will be expected to undertake other reasonable duties appropriate to the role, following suitable training and support. This job description may be reviewed as practice needs and services develop, in discussion with the postholder.

title: Senior Administrator
description: St Stephens Health Centre is seeking an experienced, proactive and highly organised Senior Administrator to join our friendly and supportive practice team. This is an important senior role within the practice, supporting the management team and providing day-to-day leadership and coordination across our administration and coding teams. The successful candidate will help ensure that administrative workflows linked to patient care are completed safely, efficiently and to a consistently high standard. The role also has a broader operational remit, supporting the Deputy Practice Manager with premises, building works, health and safety compliance and certification requirements, IT systems and service improvement. We are looking for someone who understands the demands of a busy GP practice, can confidently prioritise and delegate work, and is comfortable taking ownership of operational issues. Strong NHS primary care experience and working knowledge of EMIS Web are essential. At St Stephens Health Centre, our values of Respect, Empower and Compassion are at the heart of everything we do. If you are motivated, solutions-focused and ready to take on broader responsibility within primary care, we would welcome your application. The Senior Administrator will support the management team in coordinating the safe and effective day-to-day running of the practices administration and coding functions. The role includes providing day-to-day leadership and support to staff, coordinating rotas and leave cover, and overseeing important patient administration and coding workflows. These include document management, registrations, medical records, referrals, safeguarding administration and safety-netting processes. The postholder will also support the Deputy Practice Manager with premises and compliance responsibilities. This includes coordinating contractors and building works, maintaining health and safety documentation, risk assessments, mandatory certificates, COSHH information, asset registers, PAT testing and equipment calibration. The role requires excellent organisation, sound judgement and the ability to prioritise, delegate and respond calmly to changing demands in a busy GP practice. The Senior Administrator plays a key role in supporting the safe and effective day-to-day running of St Stephens Health Centre. Working closely with the Deputy Practice Manager and wider management team, the postholder will lead and coordinate administrative and coding functions while also supporting important operational, premises and compliance responsibilities. This is a varied and fast-paced role requiring excellent organisational skills, sound judgement, leadership capability and previous experience within primary care or an NHS setting. Oversee the day-to-day workflows of the administration and coding teams Coordinate rotas, shift cover and annual leave to maintain safe service delivery Support patient administration processes, including referrals, triaging, registrations, safeguarding workflows, medical records and results handling Coordinate coding and document-management processes, ensuring work is completed accurately and within agreed timescales Support clinical session planning, room allocation and clinician rota arrangements Provide day-to-day guidance and support to administrative staff and contribute to induction, training, recruitment and succession planning Support the Deputy Practice Manager with premises management, planned and reactive building works, contractors and maintenance requirements Help maintain health and safety documentation, risk assessments, mandatory premises certificates, COSHH records, asset registers, PAT testing and equipment calibration Monitor outstanding compliance and maintenance actions and liaise with contractors, suppliers and external services where required Support procurement, local IT and systems issues, CQC readiness and service-improvement work Provide senior operational cover across administration and reception functions when required The successful candidate will be expected to work flexibly from Monday to Friday, manage competing priorities and take ownership of delegated actions. They will need to work collaboratively across clinical and non-clinical teams.

title: GP Receptionist
description: We are looking for a friendly, reliable, enthusiastic and organised GP Receptionist to join our busy and supportive GP practice. The successful candidate will be the first point of contact for our patients and will play an important role in ensuring they receive a welcoming, professional and efficient service. We are seeking someone with excellent communication skills, a positive attitude and the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment. The ideal candidate will be compassionate, patient-focused and able to manage multiple tasks while maintaining confidentiality and professionalism. Previous experience working in a GP practice or healthcare setting would be desirable, although candidates with strong customer service and administrative experience are also encouraged to apply. This is an excellent opportunity to become part of a dedicated team committed to providing high-quality patient care and supporting the local community. The GP Receptionist will be responsible for providing efficient and professional reception and administrative support to patients, doctors and other members of the practice team. Key responsibilities include: Answering incoming telephone calls and responding to patient enquiries in a polite and professional manner. Booking, cancelling and rearranging patient appointments. Managing patient requests and assisting with the daily triage list in accordance with practice procedures. Supporting GPs and other healthcare professionals with their day-to-day administrative duties. Greeting patients and assisting them at the reception desk. Processing patient registrations and updating patient records accurately. Handling prescription requests and directing queries to the appropriate team. Managing incoming correspondence, emails and administrative tasks. Maintaining patient confidentiality and following GDPR and practice policies. Working closely with colleagues to ensure the smooth and efficient running of the practice. The successful candidate must be able to prioritise their workload, remain calm under pressure and provide excellent patient service at all times. To be responsible for undertaking a wide range of reception and administrative duties and the provision of general support to the multidisciplinary team. Duties can include but are not limited to, greeting and directing patients, patient registration, booking appointments, processing of information (electronic and hard copy) and assisting patients as required. To act as the central point of contact for patients, the distribution of information, messages and enquiries for the clinical team, liaising with multidisciplinary team members and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers.

title: GP Receptionist
description: Were looking for a friendly and motivated receptionist to join our busy practice team. title: Receptionist - GP Surgery
description: This is not for locum agencies For queries, please email i.sanghera@nhs.net Southall Medical Centre has an exciting new vacancy for a part-time (20-25 hours/week) receptionist / administrator to join our dynamic admin team! No prior GP practice experience is required, however the ideal candidate must be familiar with the role of primary care / GPs in the NHS. Good IT and computer skills are essential for this position. Key responsibilities and duties include: Triaging appointment requests and booking appointments appropriately for patients Handling incoming telephone calls to the surgery Processing repeat prescriptions according to practice policy Scanning and processing medical documents through SystmOne (clinical system) Completing tasks set by the practice manager and the doctors / clinicians Opening and closing front doors in line with opening times Greeting patients kindly and courteously Working as part of a team collaboratively with other team members Preparing the surgery, waiting area, consulting rooms in preparation for clinics You must be a friendly, courteous people-person as this role primarily involves handling patient queries and have a strong work-ethic and resolve to help provide excellent patient care, in line with our practice vision. Ability to speak Panjabi, Hindi, Gujarati or Urdu would also be extremely beneficial for this position. The role of reception / administrator is mainly an administrative role, and requires excellent people-person and communication skills, due to the patient-facing nature of the role. Duties and responsibilities of receptionists include, but are not limited to: appointments, handling telephone calls, document workflows, processing repeat prescription requests, completing tasks set by practice manager or doctors, opening/closing front doors, maintaining cleanliness of waiting area and consulting rooms, keeping noticeboards and patient areas up-to-date, working collaboratively as part of our practice team. The ideal candidate will have some experience of the NHS, however no previous GP surgery employment is required. Although you will be well-supported by our existing administrative and management team, you must be able to work independently, autonomously, with a problem-solving and can-do attitude. As the first port of call for our patients, a friendly and warm welcome and excellent communication skills are crucial to this role. The surgery is fully computerised, so good IT and computer skills are a necessity. Successful applicants will be proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) as well as SystmOne (clinical system training provided).

title: Medical Receptionist
description: We are looking for a bright, friendly, self motivated, responsible and reliable individual to join the reception team in this busy GP Surgery. title: Senior Administrator
description: We are seeking a highly organised, proactive and experienced Senior Administrator to join our busy, friendly and supportive team at Speedwell Practice. The successful candidate will play a key role in ensuring the smooth day-to-day operation of administrative services across the practice. They will lead and support the administration team while delivering efficient, patient-focused services that contribute to high standards of care, regulatory compliance and practice performance. We are looking for someone who is enthusiastic, motivated, a strong team player and willing to contribute positively to our welcoming practice environment. The role involves overseeing patient registration processes, clinical recall programmes, document management, workflow allocation, referral processing, prescription support and the maintenance of accurate patient records using EMIS Web and Docman. The post holder will also support the achievement of Quality and Outcomes Framework (QOF) targets and other contractual requirements through effective patient recall and engagement processes. As a Senior Administrator, you will act as a point of escalation for administrative queries, contribute to service improvement initiatives, support staff development and work collaboratively with clinicians, management and external agencies to ensure safe, efficient and high-quality patient care. Job Responsibilities The post holder will strive to maintain quality and efficiency within the practice and will: Provide day-to-day supervision, guidance and support to the administration team. Oversee patient registration and registration workflow processes. Manage document scanning, coding and workflow allocation using EMIS Web and Docman. Coordinate and monitor patient recall programmes, including: QOF recalls Cytology recalls Immunisation recalls NHS Health Check recalls Learning Disability recalls Diabetes recalls Other long-term condition recalls Support the management of appointment scheduling and patient communications. Process referrals, prescription requests and other clinical administration tasks. Maintain accurate and up-to-date patient records in accordance with information governance requirements. Liaise with external organisations regarding the archiving and retrieval of patient medical records. Monitor administrative performance and identify opportunities to improve efficiency and patient experience. Support the Practice Manager, Deputy Practice Manager and GP partners in achieving operational and service delivery objectives. Assist with staff training, induction and the development of administrative procedures. Support the practice in achieving QOF targets and other contractual requirements. Promote a culture of quality improvement, teamwork and patient-centred care. Alert relevant team members to issues relating to quality, safety and risk. Assess own performance and take responsibility for actions, either independently or under supervision. Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on individual and team activities and suggesting improvements. Work effectively with individuals and external agencies to meet patients' needs. Manage own time, workload and resources effectively. Participate in practice meetings and administrative team meetings as required. Participate in audits and quality improvement activities where appropriate.

title: GP Receptionist
description: We are looking for a highly motivated, flexible and reliable GP Receptionist with excellent communication skills to join our well-established, friendly, innovative, practice. This is a great opportunity to join a dynamic, and forward-thinking team. We welcome applications from experienced medical receptionists. Currently offering 9.5 h per week 2 days a week Wednesday, Thursday afternoon shifts with possible extra shifts to cover emergencies and sickness. Permanent position. Answering phones, booking appointments, answering patient's queries, chaperoning, supporting doctors and nurses in smooth running of the practice. The GP Receptionist is responsible for providing a friendly, professional and efficient front-of-house service to patients and visitors. The role involves answering telephone calls and enquiries, booking and managing appointments, registering patients, updating records and handling administrative tasks. The receptionist will liaise with GPs, nurses and other healthcare professionals to ensure patients are directed to the appropriate service. The role also requires maintaining patient confidentiality, following practice policies and procedures, handling sensitive or difficult situations appropriately, and supporting the smooth day-to-day running of the GP practice. Good communication, organisation, teamwork and customer service skills are essential.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: The Law Medical Group Practice is seeking a reliable and organised Receptionist to join the team at its Wembley branch. The practice is committed to delivering high quality primary care services to its local community and ensuring smooth day to day patient flow through efficient administrative and reception support. The successful candidate will play a key role in supporting the clinical and non clinical teams by undertaking a range of front of house and administrative duties. This will include managing appointments through EMIS, handling patient queries, processing incoming correspondence and ensuring information is accurately directed to the relevant clinicians in a timely manner. The role will involve full front of house responsibilities, including welcoming and directing patients, responding to queries and providing a professional and efficient service both in person and over the telephone. Working Pattern: Part Time, 27.5 Hours per Week The working hours are Monday to Friday, 1:00 pm to 6:30 pm. Please note: The working days and hours are non negotiable . Applicants must be able to commit to this working pattern. Eligibility: Applicants must be UK citizens and have a minimum of five years of work experience in the UK. The role involves providing comprehensive reception support to the multidisciplinary team within the practice. Key responsibilities include managing patient interactions, handling incoming correspondence, and ensuring accurate distribution of information to clinicians. The position includes front-desk duties such as greeting and directing patients, managing the appointment system using EMIS , booking appointments, responding to patient enquiries, and supporting the smooth and efficient day-to-day operation of the practice. The following are the core responsibilities of the Administrator/Receptionist . There may occasionally be a requirement to carry out other duties depending on workload, operational needs, and staffing levels. Primary Responsibilities Receive and process correspondence from hospitals, external healthcare providers, and other agencies. Scan and upload documents onto the EMIS clinical system, ensuring accurate patient record management. Review and appropriately allocate documents within EMIS , forwarding them to the relevant clinician for review and action. Initiate and respond to requests from patients, practice staff, and external healthcare agencies in a professional and timely manner. Photocopy and prepare documentation as required by clinicians and practice staff. Provide cover for colleagues during periods of absence to ensure continuity of service. Accurately input patient information and updates into EMIS where required. Manage and resolve patient queries efficiently, escalating issues where appropriate. Maintain a clean, organised, and efficient reception environment at all times. Support the clinical team with day-to-day operational tasks as required. Complete tasks relating to patient results, correspondence, and clinical letters where appropriate. Demonstrate flexibility and adaptability in managing changing workloads and priorities to ensure the smooth operation of the practice. Use EMIS and other digital systems effectively for patient record management, appointment scheduling, and internal communication. Secondary Responsibilities In addition to the primary responsibilities, the Medical Receptionist may also be required to: Maintain and monitor the practice appointment system using EMIS . Process appointment requests received in person, by telephone, and via online systems. Answer incoming telephone calls and direct them appropriately or deal with enquiries where possible. Signpost patients to the appropriate healthcare professional or NHS service. Support practice audits and administrative reviews as directed by management. Process incoming electronic communications and documents where required. Scan and attach patient-related documentation accurately to patient records within EMIS . Carry out opening and closing procedures in accordance with the practice rota and operational requirements.

Patient and Visitor Interaction Receive and direct patients, visitors, and staff in person or over the phone. Provide general assistance and answer general enquiries about services and results. title: Medical Receptionist
description: Undertake general reception and administrative duties. title: GP Receptionist

We are looking for someone reliable, organised and confident communicating with people face to face. Previous GP reception experience is an advantage, but not essential. We also welcome applicants with strong customer service experience who enjoy helping people, can manage a variety of tasks and are quick to learn new online systems. The role is 37.5 hours per week, working varied shifts between 07:45 and 18:30, Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays. Pay is £12.71 per hour. Our wider practice group offers opportunities to gain experience, develop new skills and apply for permanent positions as vacancies arise. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if sufficient applications are received. Early applications are encouraged. As a GP Receptionist, you will play an important role in supporting patients and helping the practice run smoothly. Your daily responsibilities will include: Welcoming patients and visitors, providing friendly and professional assistance. Responding to patient enquiries face to face, by telephone and through online systems. Helping patients access appropriate services, including assisting with online appointment requests. Using our clinical system (EMIS Web) and other digital platforms to manage patient information and administrative tasks. Processing patient requests, including prescriptions, test-related enquiries and general correspondence. Supporting GPs, nurses and other team members with day-to-day administrative duties. Maintaining accurate records and handling confidential information appropriately. Working closely with colleagues to provide a positive experience for patients.
