Job Description GP Receptionist Organisation: Dr Sharma & Rai Practice Group Primary Location: Heathway Medical Centre, Dagenham Contract: Full-time, fixed-term until 8 August 2027, with the possibility of extension Hours: 37.5 hours per week, with varied shifts between 07:45 and 18:30, Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays. To provide a friendly, professional and efficient reception and administrative service to patients, visitors and healthcare professionals. The GP Receptionist plays an important role in supporting patients to access healthcare services, maintaining accurate records and assisting the wider practice team with daily operations. The successful candidate will be based primarily at Heathway Medical Centre, with occasional cover at other practices within Dr Sharma & Rai Practice Group where required. 1. Patient Reception and Customer Service Welcome patients and visitors in a friendly, helpful and professional manner. Act as a first point of contact for patients attending the practice. Respond to patient enquiries face to face, by telephone and through digital communication systems. Assist patients with appointment requests and provide information about available services. Support patients who may require additional assistance accessing healthcare services. Communicate clearly and sensitively with patients from different backgrounds and with varying needs. Handle patient concerns and difficult situations calmly, professionally and respectfully, referring matters to senior colleagues when appropriate. Maintain a welcoming, organised and professional reception environment. 2. Appointment Management and Patient Access Support patients with accessing appointments and services in accordance with practice procedures. Assist patients in using online consultation and appointment request systems. Provide guidance on accessing the NHS App and other available digital services. Process appointment requests, cancellations and changes as directed by practice procedures. Signpost patients to appropriate services using established practice guidance and care navigation procedures. Escalate urgent concerns or clinical queries to the appropriate healthcare professional without providing clinical advice. Help ensure patients receive clear and accurate information about practice services. 3. Clinical Systems and Digital Administration Use EMIS Web and other practice systems to access and update patient information accurately. Process patient requests received through online platforms and electronic communication systems. Scan, upload and attach relevant documents to patient records. Record patient interactions and administrative activities appropriately. Support the processing of incoming correspondence and electronic documents. Maintain accurate records while following confidentiality and information governance requirements. Learn and confidently use new digital systems as introduced by the practice. 4. General Administrative Duties Process routine patient enquiries relating to prescriptions, test requests, referrals and other practice services in accordance with established procedures. Assist with the collection and distribution of forms, letters and other documents. Support the preparation and processing of administrative correspondence. Liaise with hospitals, pharmacies, community healthcare providers and other external organisations when required. Maintain accurate records and ensure administrative tasks are completed in a timely manner. Support clinical and non-clinical colleagues with general administrative tasks. Assist with maintaining an organised and efficient reception and office environment. 5. Teamwork and Communication Work collaboratively with reception colleagues, GPs, nurses, healthcare assistants and administrative staff. Communicate effectively with colleagues to support the smooth running of the practice. Provide reception cover and assistance to colleagues when required. Share relevant information with appropriate team members to ensure continuity of service. Participate in team meetings, training and development activities. Contribute positively to a respectful, supportive and professional working environment. 6. Confidentiality, Safety and Professional Standards Maintain strict patient confidentiality and comply with data protection and information governance requirements. Follow practice policies and procedures, including safeguarding, health and safety, infection prevention and control, and equality and diversity. Recognise and appropriately escalate safeguarding concerns or situations requiring clinical attention. Treat all patients, visitors and colleagues with dignity, respect and sensitivity. Work within the boundaries of the receptionist role and seek guidance when necessary. Maintain professional standards of conduct and appearance. Full induction and training on practice-specific systems and procedures will be provided. Previous experience in a GP practice and familiarity with EMIS Web would be advantageous but are not essential. We welcome candidates with experience in customer-facing roles who demonstrate strong communication skills, a positive attitude, good computer skills and a willingness to learn. As part of Dr Sharma & Rai Practice Group, employees may have opportunities to develop additional skills, gain experience across different practice functions and apply for permanent vacancies as they arise. The successful candidate must be flexible in their working hours and available for different shifts within the practice's core opening hours. This job description outlines the main responsibilities of the position and may be reviewed or adapted to meet the operational needs of the practice, within the appropriate scope of the role.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: Abbey Medical Centre Camden, London NW8 OAG. We are seeking committed receptionists, who demonstrate enthusiasm for working in primary care, with a genuine interest in working with patients and contributing to the delivery of high quality health care. Applicants should be courteous, highly motivated, pro-active and good team players, able to project a positive and friendly image to patients/visitors. These posts are full time/part time . Each of the posts available may be suitable for job share. Part Time will also be considered (over 5 days). This will involve working on reception (front desk), back office function including processing repeat prescriptions, scanning, summarising, filing medical records.etc. The job will be varied and time will be split between the roles. The surgery uses EMISWeb/DOCMAN 10 as their clinical system. The following are the core responsibilities of the receptionist/administrator. There may be on occasion, a requirement to carry out other tasks; this will be dependent upon factors such as workload and staffing levels: a. Maintaining and monitoring the practice appointment system b. Process personal, telephone and e-requests for appointments c. Answer incoming phone calls, transferring calls or dealing with the callers request appropriately d. Action all incoming faxes e. Signpost patients to the correct service f. Process incoming and outgoing mail g. Initiating contact with and responding to, requests from patients, team members and external agencies h. Process referrals to external agencies such as secondary care using the electronic referral system (ERS) i. Process calling letters are requested j. Process all DNA letters in accordance with current policy k. Action GP2GP tasks l. Read code data on EMIS Web m. Photocopy documentation as required n. File and store records as required o. Data entry of new and temporary registrations and relevant patient information as required p. Input data into the patients healthcare records as necessary q. Scanning of patient related documentation and attaching scanned documents to patients healthcare records r. Process requests for information i.e. SAR, insurance / solicitors letters and DVLA forms to the administrative team s. Manage all queries (including administrative queries) as necessary in an efficient manner t. Carry out system searches as requested u. Maintain a clean, tidy, effective working area at all times v. Monitor and maintain the reception area and notice boards w. Support all clinical staff with general tasks as requested Secondary Responsibilities In addition to the primary responsibilities, the medical administrator may be requested to: a. Partake in audit as directed by the audit lead b. Produce meeting agendas and record the minutes of meetings c. Support administrative and reception staff, providing cover during staff absences d. Complete opening and closing procedures in accordance with the duty rota e. As required support in the management of repeat prescriptions, ensuring they are processed accurately and efficiently f. Ordering and monitoring of stationery supplies
